frontal_bone.name: Frontal Bone
frontal_bone.description: The bone of the forehead. It forms the front of the skull and the roofs of the eye sockets.
facts: Contains the frontal sinuses, air spaces above the eyes.
At birth it is in two halves that usually fuse in early childhood.
Meets the parietal bones at the coronal suture.

parietal_bones.name: Parietal Bones
parietal_bones.description: A pair of bones that form the top and upper sides of the skull.
facts: The two parietal bones meet in the midline at the sagittal suture.
They meet the occipital bone at the lambdoid suture.
They protect the upper part of the brain.

temporal_bones.name: Temporal Bones
temporal_bones.description: A pair of bones on the sides and base of the skull, around the ears.
facts: House the middle and inner ear, including the tiny ear bones.
Form the joint with the lower jaw (temporomandibular joint).
The mastoid process behind the ear is part of the temporal bone.

occipital_bone.name: Occipital Bone
occipital_bone.description: The bone at the back and base of the skull.
facts: Has a large opening, the foramen magnum, where the spinal cord joins the brainstem.
Its occipital condyles form the joint with the first neck vertebra (atlas).
Protects the back of the brain, including the visual areas.

sphenoid_bone.name: Sphenoid Bone
sphenoid_bone.description: A butterfly-shaped bone in the middle of the skull base that links many other skull bones.
facts: Touches every other bone of the cranium.
Contains the sella turcica, a hollow that holds the pituitary gland.
Forms part of the eye sockets and has the sphenoid sinuses inside.

ethmoid_bone.name: Ethmoid Bone
ethmoid_bone.description: A light, spongy bone between the eye sockets that forms part of the nasal cavity.
facts: Its cribriform plate has small holes for the smell (olfactory) nerves.
Contains the ethmoid air cells (sinuses).
Forms the upper part of the nasal septum.

zygomatic_bones.name: Zygomatic Bones
zygomatic_bones.description: The cheekbones. They form the prominence of the cheeks and part of the eye sockets.
facts: Join the temporal bone to form the zygomatic arch.
Form the outer wall and floor of each eye socket.
Also called the malar bones.

maxillae.name: Maxillae (Upper Jaw)
maxillae.description: A pair of bones that fuse to form the upper jaw, holding the upper teeth.
facts: Form most of the hard palate (roof of the mouth), together with the palatine bones.
Contain the maxillary sinuses, the largest of the paranasal sinuses.
Form part of the floor of the eye sockets and the walls of the nasal cavity.

nasal_bones.name: Nasal Bones
nasal_bones.description: Two small bones that form the bridge of the nose.
facts: The lower part of the nose is cartilage, not bone.
They are among the most commonly broken facial bones.

lacrimal_bones.name: Lacrimal Bones
lacrimal_bones.description: The smallest bones of the face, in the inner wall of each eye socket.
facts: Help form the channel that drains tears from the eye into the nose.
Each is about the size of a fingernail.

palatine_bones.name: Palatine Bones
palatine_bones.description: L-shaped bones at the back of the nasal cavity that form the rear part of the hard palate.
facts: Form the back part of the roof of the mouth.
Also help form the floor of the eye sockets and the walls of the nasal cavity.

vomer.name: Vomer
vomer.description: A thin, flat bone that forms the lower and back part of the nasal septum.
facts: Named after the Latin word for ploughshare because of its shape.
Divides the nasal cavity into left and right sides together with the ethmoid and cartilage.

mandible.name: Mandible (Lower Jaw)
mandible.description: The lower jaw, the largest and strongest bone of the face and the only skull bone that moves freely.
facts: Holds the lower teeth.
Forms the temporomandibular joint with the temporal bone on each side.
Its two halves fuse at the chin in the first year of life.

hyoid_bone.name: Hyoid Bone
hyoid_bone.description: A U-shaped bone in the neck below the jaw that supports the tongue.
facts: It does not touch any other bone; it is held in place by muscles and ligaments.
Helps with swallowing and speaking.
It is not part of the skull itself but is often studied with it.
